newsitem.title: BELARUS: Police detain more journalists in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Police detain more journalists in Belarus.

text.p: Police on Thursday detained 14 journalists in the Belarussian capital Minsk who were taking part in and reporting on presentation of a petition in support of an arrested Russian television crew, witnesses said.

A Reuters correspondent was among those detained and filed a brief report by telephone from the building where he was being held. Other reporters and cameramen from Belarussian and foreign media were also taken in by police.

Several dozen reporters staged a protest demanding the release of a crew from Public Russian Television (ORT) who face up to five years in prison after authorities charged them with illegally crossing the Belarussian-Lithuanian border.
Journalists picketed Minsk's KGB security service building and the Interior Ministry before moving to the headquarters of the administration of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.

Police closed in on both the protesting journalists and reporters covering the action, as the protesters tried to hand in their petition to Lukashenko's office. One witness said one correspondent was beaten by police.

The detention of the ORT crew at the weekend sparked a war of words between Moscow and Minsk and a protest from human rights group Amnesty International. Journalists have frequently been detained in Minsk during opposition rallies, but often they are quickly fined and released.
